title: Neutrogena breaks silence following backlash after Hayden Panettiere’s death
author: Carsen Holaday
content:
![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/6b1f2958d5ab456d93026ec1af388c7ac26b77b35f0efc754587cb9fb37da797/lightyear_networkapi/resizefill_w640%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fthe_independent_video_898%2F0a7373082c6679a4078c437e918929aa.jpg)
Neutrogena has broken its silence about former ambassador Hayden Panettiere's death following days of backlash against the skincare brand over its treatment of the late actor.
Panettiere was found dead Sunday at age 36, prompting interviews and comments from the Nashville star to resurface, including her remarks earlier this year that Neutrogena "fired" her in 2015 after she spoke about her postpartum depression.
"We are deeply saddened by Hayden Panettiere's passing," Neutrogena said in a statement posted to its social media accounts Thursday. "For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community."
"We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be," the statement continued.
Neutrogena vowed to make a "significant investment to a long-standing community health partner" to support women's health causes and promised to share more details "when plans are in place."
![Neutrogena has spoken out about the death of former ambassador Hayden Panettiere (PA Archive)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/f5b7c318e9cff43e0e1534e5d358266c024767d95c513cecf0f0dccbba126598/lightyear_networkapi/resizefill_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fthe_independent_577%2Fb52bb7c60046437b5453d8d35c869b4e.jpg)
Neutrogena has spoken out about the death of former ambassador Hayden Panettiere (PA Archive)
"Out of respect for Hayden's family and loved ones, we did not want to speak out so soon following her passing. Everyone at Neutrogena extends their deepest condolences to Hayden's family and all who loved her."
The Independent has reached out to Neutrogena for further comment.
Although the comments are turned off on the new post, Neutrogena's previous posts are flooded with comments criticizing the brand, demanding justice for Panettiere and urging customers to boycott the company.
The Heroes star wrote in her 2026 memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning that the company severed ties with her after she spoke publicly about receiving mental health treatment for postpartum depression following the birth of her daughter, Kaya, in 2014, saying: "Neutrogena canceled my long-standing contract, and it was yet another blow in a year that had given almost nothing else."
![Panettiere was the face of Neutrogena for about 10 years (Neutrogena)](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/409910a5c993b9003b26ea10c3f381bfd3f96a74e7799325804e398b067ecbd0/lightyear_networkapi/resizefill_w960%3Bquality_80%3Bformat_webp/https%3A%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fthe_independent_577%2Ff29c4ab424d4f770d90ba098671dafab.jpg)
Panettiere was the face of Neutrogena for about 10 years (Neutrogena)
In one of her final podcast appearances in the months before her death, Panettiere told podcaster Jay Shetty in May that she was surprised when her representative told her that her remarks about PPD had broken her contract's morality clause.
"Neutrogena was a huge part of my life," Panettiere recalled. "I had the morals clauses, they caught absolutely everything. And of all the things that they would fire me over, this is the last thing that I thought they would ever fire me for."
"So when I got that call that Neutrogena wanted to fire me over that, my representative at the time said, 'That's illegal. You can't do that,'" Panettiere said. "Even though she saved the day that year, I knew that that was going to be it. I was not going to be invited back the next year."
Panettiere's cause of death has not been disclosed.
If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.
If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.
This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you
summary: Neutrogena has issued a statement addressing criticism over its past treatment of former brand ambassador Hayden Panettiere, who passed away at age 36. Following her death, resurfaced remarks revealed that Panettiere stated the company fired her in 2015 for speaking publicly about her postpartum depression. Neutrogena acknowledged that they made her feel unsupported during a difficult time and announced plans to invest in women's health causes.
key_points: Neutrogena released a statement addressing backlash regarding its past treatment of Hayden Panettiere.
Panettiere previously stated that Neutrogena dropped her in 2015 after she spoke about postpartum depression.
Neutrogena acknowledged that they made Panettiere feel unsupported during a difficult time.
The skincare brand pledged to make a significant investment in women's health causes.

title: What happened to Harry and Meghan's American dream?
author: Shaimaa Khalil; Regan Morris
content:
Watch: How Harry and Meghan are ending their 'American dream'
- Published
When the Duke and Duchess of Sussex quit working for the Royal Family in 2020 and moved to California, they brought something even Hollywood can't manufacture: royalty.
But while Harry and Meghan enjoyed some success in showbusiness, their Hollywood reign proved short-lived and California has greeted news of their departure back to the UK with a shrug.
In pursuing their American dream, they said they were seeking more than financial independence.
In their 2021 blockbuster interview with Oprah Winfrey, Meghan described the freedom to make her own choices as "liberating".
Harry later said America offered his family a degree of privacy and freedom they "undoubtedly wouldn't be able" to enjoy in the UK - and that it was the life his mother, Diana, would have wanted for him.
The couple settled in Montecito - a celebrity enclave a few hours north of Los Angeles with neighbours like Oprah Winfrey, Gwyneth Paltrow and Rob Lowe.
Multimillion dollar podcast and Netflix deals followed.
"They were so sought after, they were names that would hit the press and command attention right away," says Stacy Jones, chief executive of Hollywood Branded, a marketing and PR agency.
![Harry and Meghan smiling next to two others, wearing cocktail attire, at a house](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/907/cpsprodpb/54f8/live/3968b500-9cf5-11f1-8cdc-014599ccd660.jpg)
Harry and Meghan with Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos and wife Nicole Avant
"There are endless parties, endless events and endless things to do if you are a celebrity inside Hollywood," she says. "But you soon realise that all those endless things are promoting something to sell."
And the royal couple had plenty to sell.
LA-based royal watcher and journalist Elizabeth Holmes, who wrote HRH: So Many Thoughts on Royal Style, says: "I think part of why this [the Sussexes leaving the US] was surprising to me was just because it did feel like they were sort of settling into their life in California."
Californians reacts to Harry and Meghan's return to the UK
Not everyone is sad to see them go. The New York Post, often scathing about the couple, greeted the news of their departure with the headline "Throne Back!", declaring that America's "long national nightmare is over".
The tabloid mockery was largely dismissive of the couple's rare achievement in Hollywood. They managed something most newcomers to Tinseltown never do: persuading some of its biggest companies to invest heavily in them.
Attracting that initial investment proved easier than sustaining it, however.
Their multi-year Spotify deal, reported to be worth up to $25m (Â£18.3m), produced Meghan's 12-episode podcast Archetypes, featuring guests such as Serena Williams and Mariah Carey.
In 2023, however, Spotify and the couple's Archewell Audio announced that they had "mutually agreed to part ways".
Their five-year Netflix deal, signed in 2020 and reportedly worth between $60m and $100m, delivered several programmes.
But it has since been replaced by a less lucrative arrangement, against the backdrop of a broader downturn across the entertainment industry.
Behind the projects, the Sussexes' production business also experienced high staff turnover, with reports that some former employees privately called themselves the "Sussex Survivors Club".
Harry, too, found commercial success, but largely when he was selling his own royal story.
His memoir, Spare, was a publishing phenomenon, reportedly coming with a $20m advance.
It sold more than six million copies worldwide, making it the fastest-selling non-fiction book on record.
As part of its promotion, Harry held a public conversation with trauma specialist Dr Gabor MatÃ©, in which he explored how his royal childhood had shaped him.
In an interview with BBC Newsnight on Thursday, MatÃ© said Harry had come across as "very personable, very sensitive" and someone doing his best to make sure "he doesn't pass on his traumas to his children".
Watch: Trauma expert unpacks Harry and Meghan's return to the UK
The Duke of Sussex remains enormously marketable when the subject is Harry himself, the Royal Family or the causes with which he has long been associated.
He became chief impact officer at the Silicon Valley coaching company BetterUp and co-created and executive-produced the Apple TV+ mental-health series The Me You Can't See, with Oprah Winfrey.
His Netflix projects have drawn heavily on his established interests.
Heart of Invictus followed wounded and injured military veterans preparing for the Games he founded, while Polo explored another of his passions.
Neither attracted anything approaching the attention generated by the couple's six-part documentary series Harry & Meghan, or his revelations in Spare.
In one of his relatively rare major public appearances, Harry also delivered the keynote address at an informal meeting of the UN General Assembly in New York in 2022, marking Nelson Mandela International Day. He spoke about his mother, his connection to Africa and Mandela's legacy.
But he seemed to struggle to break out of his royal typecast role in the US.
![a close-up photo of Harry and Meghan laughing with a dog in between them](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/7130/live/556a36d0-9cf9-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The couple had their own Netflix documentary series called Harry & Meghan
As for former Suits actress Meghan, she branched out into a Netflix cooking and lifestyle series.
This content showed off their idyllic life with adorable "rescue chickens" and fresh-grown strawberries, against the scenic backdrop of the Santa Ynez Mountains.
With Love, Meghan was cancelled after two seasons, but it has been nominated for an Emmy in the Outstanding Lifestyle Series category.
Netflix also ended its involvement in Meghan's lifestyle brand, As Ever, earlier this year.
"Netflix produces movies. Netflix doesn't produce jam," says Jones, the brand guru.
![a phone screen showing "With Love, Meghan" series page on Netflix, in front of a TV with the show playing](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/6f59/live/de87f2f0-9cf8-11f1-a07e-5d2ec7b46104.jpg)
Meghan displayed a highly curated version of herself on her Netflix show With Love, Meghan
Critics assailed the carefully curated lifestyle presented by Meghan as tone-deaf. But in branding terms, Jones acknowledges that even negative publicity can have value if it keeps someone at the centre of the conversation.
Meghan's projects kept her visible and gave audiences something they could watch or buy.
"In moving to Britain, it looks like they are continuing to chase that proximity to the Royal Family to validate themselves or, in some cases, to commercialise," says Kinsey Schofield, whose namesake podcast focuses on the Royal Family.
"Meghan's been cosplaying as a royal selling her teas and her fruit spread through As Ever since it launched."
The Sussexes still have projects in development. They recently released a documentary about Girl Scouts and they have a scripted series in the works set in the exclusive world of polo teams, to be produced by the makers of Gossip Girl.
But their American experience overall reveals the limits of celebrity in Hollywood.
Fame may get you through the door, but it does not guarantee staying power.
![Harry and Meghan standing beside each in the stands of a baseball game, both wearing Dodgers hat, with Meghan cheering](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/0d34/live/1f988df0-9cf8-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Harry and Meghan attending a Los Angeles Dodgers game in October 2025
"Hollywood is going through an incredibly hard time right now, and it's a fractured landscape," Jones says.
Layoffs, repeated restructuring and high staff turnover have destabilised companies across the industry.
"It is pretty hard to start and launch a company and keep it going," she says. "When that company is being launched by someone who is a mega media star, it needs some really strong people supporting it."
They may no longer occupy the position they held when they first arrived in America, and they may say they're heading back to the UK to be private citizens, but it's unlikely that the couple would fade in the background.
"They will never be private citizens anywhere in their lives," Jones says.
"They are not people who can ever become background players. They are stars of their own show - or stars of someone else's show. Even if they're lower-level stars, they're still stars."
summary: After moving to California in 2020 following their departure from the Royal Family, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle secured major Hollywood deals, but ultimately struggled to sustain their initial commercial success. Despite achieving high-profile projects like Harry's bestselling memoir Spare and various media ventures, the couple faced contract changes, show cancellations, and high staff turnover. As they prepare to return to the UK, their American experience highlights the difficulties of maintaining long-term staying power in the entertainment industry.
key_points: Harry and Meghan moved to California in 2020 seeking financial independence, privacy, and freedom.
The couple secured lucrative multi-million dollar deals with companies like Netflix and Spotify, though some partnerships ended or were scaled back over time.
Harry achieved significant commercial success primarily when focusing on his royal background, notably with his record-breaking memoir Spare.
Meghan's lifestyle and cooking series, With Love, Meghan, was cancelled after two seasons, and Netflix ended its involvement with her lifestyle brand, As Ever.
Industry experts noted that while initial fame helped the couple secure high-profile investments, sustaining long-term success in Hollywood proved challenging.

title: We can all learn a valuable lesson from Anthony Hopkins’s new album
author: Louis Chilton
content:
The history of music is littered with the detritus of Hollywood’s vanity. Many an A-list actor has convinced themselves they’ve got the goods to make it as a musician, be that Eddie Murphy, Bruce Willis, or Robert Downey Jr. The results are seldom good. To this end, you might have reason to hoist an eyebrow when you spot Sir Anthony Hopkins is releasing an album this week. But how wrong you’d be.
Life is a Dream is the second record from the Oscar-winning star of The Silence of the Lambs and The Father. (His previous album, Composer, was released on CD in 2012, through Classic FM.) Those who might be bewildered by the mental image of the 88-year-old Welshman strutting a stage like Mick Jagger singing “Sympathy for the Devil” need not worry: these are classical compositions, composed by Hopkins over the course of his life and performed by the Philharmonia Orchestra with Grammy Award-winning conductor Gustavo Dudamel.
There is something wonderfully, life-affirmingly sweet about this music, which shifts between classical forms, from bright, brass-led fanfares to elegant waltzes. It would be easy to sound patronising about Hopkins’s passion project, were it not for the fact that it is legitimately good. There is more music artistry on show here than in many of today’s charting pop releases – albeit in service of a genre that gets scant shrift in the mainstream. Hopkins has a pleasing grasp of harmony and an ear for flighty melody; in the spectrum of classical music, it’s on the more traditional side, absent of the dissonance and tonal complexity that the 20th century brought to the genre.
Life is a Dream is a personal thing for Hopkins; that much is evident in the music’s wordless sentimentality. Some of the tracks are inspired by his native Wales, including “1947: Suite for Solo Piano and Orchestra: II. Bracken Road”, which he wrote in 1963 while working as a young actor at the Liverpool Playhouse. Hopkins began learning the piano at the age of four, and has written music since he was a child, describing music as “my first desire” and “my first wish”. Several of his compositions have been performed before in concert halls around the world; renowned conductor André Rieu recorded a waltz by Hopkins on his 2011 album And the Waltz Goes On; that work also features here.
![From ‘Elephant Man’ to music man: Anthony Hopkins in the studio](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/20/16/15/AnthonyHopkins_Credit-Charlie-Gray-2.jpeg)
To some extent, hearing Hopkins’s music simply confirms what everyone has always known about him. Whatever the project – even while playing sociopathic cannibal Hannibal Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs – he radiates sophistication and sincerity. On some level, it simply makes sense that Hopkins is able to compose such moving, edifying music: it’s an extension of what he’s been doing his whole career.
When a wealthy celebrity, respected in their field, decides to venture out and try their hand in another, it’s hard to escape the whiff of egocentrism. We do not expect these things to be good, or particularly meaningful; they are referred to as “side projects” for a reason. It’s a credit both to Hopkins’ craft and his judgement that such dismissals fall away while actually listening to Life is a Dream. It is honest music made for the right reasons. In a way, he can be as proud of this as he can of any of his screen performances – and he probably is.
What’s more, for Hopkins to do this at 88 is nothing short of inspirational. If there’s a lesson here, it’s that life doesn’t stop when you hit 60, or 70, or 80. (Or even when you become the oldest actor to ever win an Oscar, at the age of 83.) There’s always something more to do. There’s always more music, waiting to be played.
‘Life is a Dream’ is out now on Decca Classics
summary: Oscar-winning actor Sir Anthony Hopkins is releasing his second classical music album, titled Life is a Dream. Composed by Hopkins over the course of his life and performed by the Philharmonia Orchestra, the traditional classical compositions have been praised for their genuine artistry and emotional sentiment. The release serves as an inspiring reminder that creative pursuits can continue at any age.
key_points: Sir Anthony Hopkins is releasing a classical music album titled Life is a Dream on Decca Classics.
The album features classical compositions written by Hopkins over his life and performed by the Philharmonia Orchestra.
Hopkins has composed music since childhood and previously released an album titled Composer in 2012.
The music includes traditional classical forms, with some tracks inspired by his native Wales.

title: Anthony Hopkins: Life Is a Dream album review – easy on the ear melodies written from the heart
author: Clive Paget
content:
Anthony Hopkins has, it turns out, has been composing music all his life. Now, at the age of 88, the Welsh-born Hollywood actor makes his Decca debut, securing the services of LA Philharmonic’s outgoing music director Gustavo Dudamel to bring his music to life.
![Life Is a Dream: Music Composed by Anthony Hopkins, album cover](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/75c4ea7958aee58ed0adc44aeee43b5caaa00cdb/0_0_3000_3000/master/3000.jpg?width=120&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
So, what does an Oscar winner sound like? Not surprisingly, there’s a significant cinematic influence, inspired by the music that caught the attention of a lad growing up in Margam, a suburb of Port Talbot. The opening Fanfare and March is a catchy, Technicolor splash, like everything here harmonious and written from the heart. Ditto the Khachaturian-flavoured Two Pieces for Orchestra. Welsh roots are honoured too: My Fatherland, featuring six traditional tunes, four sung in Welsh, would not seem out of place at the Last Night of the Proms.
Reminiscences abound, including the lively 1947: Suite for Orchestra recalling one of the hottest summers on record. It takes its cue from the streets and mountains surrounding Hopkins’ childhood home, including an unforgettable visit with his father to the Plaza cinema. Then there are works dedicated to his wife (Stella Aria and the Stanley Myers-inspired Farewell My Love) and his niece (Tara).
Soloists are distinguished – Argentinian pianist Sergio Tiempo and Venezuelan cellist Gregorio Nieto – with fine contributions from the Philharmonia Orchestra and the Bach Choir. The spacious recording is state-of-the-art. Those who appreciate easy-on-the-ear melody and good old-fashioned craft should find plenty to enjoy.

summary: At the age of 88, Oscar-winning actor Anthony Hopkins is releasing his debut album with Decca, titled "Life Is a Dream," featuring compositions brought to life by conductor Gustavo Dudamel. The album reflects Hopkins's cinematic influences, Welsh heritage, and personal reminiscences dedicated to his family and childhood. Supported by distinguished soloists and the Philharmonia Orchestra, the release offers harmonious, easy-on-the-ear melodies written from the heart.
key_points: Anthony Hopkins makes his Decca debut with the album "Life Is a Dream" at the age of 88.
The music features strong cinematic influences and honors Hopkins's Welsh roots.
Several tracks serve as personal reminiscences and are dedicated to his wife and niece.
The album features performances by distinguished soloists, the Philharmonia Orchestra, and the Bach Choir.

title: Brian Hickerson issues first statement since Hayden Panettiere’s death: Latest
author: Shahana Yasmin; Caitlin Hornik
content:
Hayden Panettiere, who became a household name as a teenager for her role in Heroes and later starred in Nashville and multiple Scream films, has died at age 36.
Panettiere was pronounced dead at a South Carolina apartment Sunday, August 16. A cause of death has not been revealed, but an autopsy showed no signs of trauma. Toxicology reports are pending and could take up to 12 weeks, according to the Greenville County Coroner’s Office.
An investigation is reportedly being conducted into Panettiere’s death involving Greenville police as well as the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration after an incident report stated that her on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, turned over a “bag of medication” to police.
Panettiere was best-known for playing Sheryl Yoast in the 2000 Denzel Washington-led film Remember the Titans, high school cheerleader Claire Bennet on NBC’s sci-fi drama Heroes (2006-2010), and aspiring country singer Juliette Barnes on the hit TV series Nashville (2012-2018).
Her New York Times bestselling memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, was published in May this year, in which she looked back at her childhood in Hollywood and her experiences with addiction, postpartum depression (which she claimed cost her a sponsorship with skincare brand Neutrogena), abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of her daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with former heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko.
Hayden Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson breaks silence
Brian Hickerson has broken his silence following Hayden Panettiere’s death, issuing his first statement through his lawyer, Sloan Ellis.
“Hayden’s death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed,” Ellis said in a statement to TMZ. “As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play.”
The statement added: “Out of respect for Hayden’s loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time.”
Hickerson, who had an on-and-off relationship with Panettiere, was at the apartment when Panettiere was found unresponsive on Sunday, along with his brother Zach. He showed responding officers a bag of medication Panettiere had been taking, while authorities later said an autopsy found no signs of trauma.
The DEA has since joined the investigation, and Panettiere’s cause and manner of death remain pending.
Hickerson also has a history of domestic violence against Panettiere and pleaded no contest to two felony charges involving her in 2021.
Neutrogena breaks silence after backlash
Panettiere’s death prompted the actor’s previous comments about how she was “fired” from being the face of the brand for speaking out about her postpartum depression to resurface.
“We are deeply saddened by Hayden Panettiere’s passing,” the company said in a statement posted to its social media accounts. “For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community.”
“We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time. This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be,” the statement continued.
Read more:
Hayden Panettiere said she was focused on ‘finding meaning in life’ months before her death
Hayden Panettiere spoke about finding purpose in her life and looking towards new creative opportunities just months before her death.
“I know that if I surround myself with positive people, I can accomplish whatever I set my mind to,” she told The Independent in May, and said she wanted to write and produce, and release a jewellery line.
“I’ve made my share of mistakes, I’ve fallen on my face, but I’ve always stood up again and dusted myself off.”
She added: “I’ve got plenty of issues, but finding meaning in life isn’t one of them.”
Panettiere said creativity had provided a “lifeline” and given her purpose when she needed it most.
![](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/05/21/14/50/HAYDEN-PANETTIERE-2-credit-Storm-Santos.jpeg?trim=0,0,0,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
Hayden Panettiere would have celebrated her 37th birthday today
Hayden Panettiere would have turned 37 today, just five days after the actor died suddenly at the age of 36.
Panettiere was born on 21 August 1989 and died on 16 August in South Carolina. She was said to have been looking forward to spending her birthday with her 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, in Germany.
A source close to the actor told Page Six that she had been “so excited to see her” and had been telling people how much she was looking forward to spending time with her daughter.
Panettiere's memoir This Is Me: A Reckoning was published in May, in which she wrote openly about her childhood in Hollywood, addiction, postpartum depression, abusive relationships, and the loss of custody of Kaya.
The heartbreaking family struggles that shaped Hayden Panettiere’s life off screen
The ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville’ star, who has tragically died aged 36, was bracingly honest about her experiences of familial estrangement, losing custody of her daughter and the depression that followed the sudden death of her younger brother, writes Katie Rosseinsky
![](https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/17/7/14/Screenshot-2026-08-17-at-08-56-49.png?trim=0,0,95,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800)
Hayden Panettiere was a passionate advocate of Ukraine
Panettiere’s daughter moved to Ukraine to live with her father, boxer Wladimir Klitschko, in 2018, when Russia had illegally annexed Crimea in 2014 and separatist forces were fighting Ukrainian troops in the Donbas region.
When Vladimir Putin launched his full-scale invasion in February 2022, Klitschko, whose brother Vitalii is the mayor of Kyiv and also a former boxing champion, enlisted in the army. Kaya, the outlet reported, was not in Ukraine from the early days of the war.
Panettiere posted repeated messages of solidarity with Ukraine on Instagram in the years that followed.
“I have personally witnessed the strength of the Ukrainian people who fought so hard for their independence and have continued to passionately defend their country over the years. What Putin is doing is an absolute disgrace!,” she wrote on Instagram shortly after the invasion.
“This horrific moment in history sends a terrifying message: the message that in this day and age, in year 2022, it’s okay to violate the rights of free people and allow autocrats like Putin to take whatever they please,” she added.
Ice Princess director recalls Hayden Panettiere as ‘plucky and determined’
Ice Princess director Tim Fywell has paid tribute to Hayden Panettiere, recalling the actor’s dedication while making the 2005 Disney film alongside Michelle Trachtenberg.
“It was really upsetting to hear yesterday of the death of Hayden Panettiere at the age of 36,” Fywell said in a statement to Variety. “I remember a brave, sparky, dedicated young actress who lit up the set in rehearsals and then the screen with her vibrant talent.”
Panettiere played Gen Harwood, a talented figure skater and rival to Michelle Trachtenberg’s Casey Carlyle, a science student who discovers a passion for skating.
![Hayden Panettiere and Michelle Trachtenberg in Ice Princess](<https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/17/9/45/Hayden-Panettiere-and-Michelle-Trachtenberg-from-Ice-Princess-(2005).jpeg>)
Fywell described the two as “an amazing pair”, remembering Panettiere as “plucky and determined and perfectionist” who spent hours practising her skating and was “utterly focused on getting every acting take spot-on and truthful”.
“In what was often a tough and technically complicated shoot, and my first Hollywood movie, they were delightful to work with and great to have around,” he said. “I remember them both with huge affection, how they were 20 odd years ago, at that relatively uncomplicated time of their lives, two shining talents, gone far too soon.”
‘We made her feel unsupported’: Neutrogena responds after Hayden Panettiere’s death
Neutrogena has addressed criticism over its treatment of Hayden Panettiere, saying it understands that the actor felt “unsupported” during a difficult period in her life.
The skincare brand said in a statement on Thursday: “We are deeply saddened by Hayden Panettiere’s passing. For more than a decade, Hayden was a valued member of our Neutrogena community.”
“We are proud to have partnered with her and understand that we made her feel unsupported during a very difficult time,” it continued. “This is not what Neutrogena stands for or who we want to be.”
Neutrogena vowed to make a “significant investment to a long-standing community health partner” to support women’s health causes and promised to share more details “when plans are in place.”
Panettiere wrote in her memoir that Neutrogena cancelled her long-standing contract in 2015 after she spoke publicly about her postpartum depression. In a May interview with Jay Shetty, she said: “Of all the things that they would fire me over, this is the last thing that I thought they would ever fire me for.”
Ice Princess director remembers Panettiere and Michelle Trachtenberg
Tim Fywell, who directed Disney’s beloved 2005 ice skating movie Ice Princess, has reflected on the tragic fact that both of the film’s star have now died prematurely.
In a statement to Variety, Fywell said: “It was really upsetting to hear yesterday of the death of Hayden Panettiere at the age of 36. I remember a brave, sparky, dedicated young actress who lit up the set in rehearsals and then the screen with her vibrant talent. Michelle Trachtenberg, Hayden’s co-star in the movie, and she were an amazing pair.”
Fywell added that the pair had “very different personalities.” While Trachtenberg was “kooky, fun, with an infectious laugh and her brilliant sad-funny comic timing,” Panettiere was “plucky and determined and perfectionist, spending hours practicing her skating and utterly focused on getting every acting take spot-on and truthful. Which she did.”
Fywell concluded: “In what was often a tough and technically complicated shoot, and my first Hollywood movie, they were delightful to work with and great to have around. I remember them both with huge affection, how they were 20 odd years ago, at that relatively uncomplicated time of their lives, two shining talents, gone far too soon.”
![](<https://static.the-independent.com/2026/08/17/9/45/Hayden-Panettiere-and-Michelle-Trachtenberg-from-Ice-Princess-(2005).jpeg?trim=23,0,23,0&width=1200&height=800&crop=1200:800>)
Director says Hayden Panettiere was ‘fighting to stay sober’ before her death
Director Griff Furst has claimed Hayden Panettiere was “fighting to stay sober” while filming his 2025 movie A Breed Apart and he was asked to participate in an intervention.
“I was rooting for Hayden to beat the addiction that she spoke about openly and publicly,” Furst said in an Instagram video. He added that “no matter how certain you are that an actor or crew member is in a bad situation”, a producer or director can’t do much besides adjusting the schedule or getting a handler “to make sure that that individual is being taken care of as best as they can”.
He said he remained in contact with Panettiere’s team during filming, which led to him being asked to join the proposed intervention.
“I was asked to participate, and I said yes,” Furst claimed. “That intervention did not happen, at least not that I am aware of. I wasn’t leading the charge on it. It wouldn’t have been appropriate for me.”
Furst previously said Panettiere was accompanied by her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson on the set and that she “deserved better company” around her.
summary: Actor Hayden Panettiere has died at age 36 in South Carolina, prompting an ongoing investigation by police and the DEA. Her on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, issued a statement through his lawyer noting that the death is under investigation and that there were no signs of foul play. Meanwhile, skincare brand Neutrogena and various colleagues have released statements offering tributes and addressing past challenges in her life and career.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere passed away at age 36 in a South Carolina apartment, with toxicology reports and an official cause of death still pending.
Brian Hickerson issued his first statement through his lawyer, confirming that the death remains under investigation and that police found no signs of foul play.
Neutrogena released a statement acknowledging that they made Panettiere feel unsupported after she spoke publicly about postpartum depression.
Panettiere's recent memoir, published in May, addressed her struggles with addiction, postpartum depression, and abusive relationships.

title: British rapper Yung Filly to face retrial on rape charges in Australia
author: Katy Watson
content:
![Yung Filly, wearing a cream hoodie](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/663b/live/8f14ea70-9d16-11f1-acd5-9b942218313f.jpg)
- Published
British rapper Yung Filly will face a retrial on three rape charges in Australia, after a jury cleared him of several sexual assault offences but could not reach a decision on others.
The YouTuber, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, was charged with repeatedly raping and assaulting a fan after performing at a nightclub in Perth in 2024.
He denied all 10 charges, and last month a jury found him not guilty on three counts of sexual penetration without consent.
He was also acquitted of one assault charge and another of strangulation, but was found guilty of two counts of assault occasioning bodily harm, for which he'll be sentenced after his retrial.
The West Australian court heard that the 31-year-old social media star had consensual sex with a 20-year-old fan in his hotel room, before she alleged he turned violent and ignored her cries to stop.
Barrientos will next appear in court 27 August for an application to vary his bail. A retrial date has not been set.

summary: British rapper and YouTuber Yung Filly will face an Australian retrial on three rape charges after a jury failed to reach a verdict on those counts. He was cleared of several other sexual assault and violence charges, but was found guilty of two counts of assault occasioning bodily harm. The charges stem from an incident in Perth in 2024 involving a 20-year-old fan.
key_points: Yung Filly's real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos.
He was found guilty of two counts of assault occasioning bodily harm.
A jury cleared him of three counts of sexual penetration without consent, one assault charge, and one strangulation charge.
He will appear in court on 27 August for a bail variation application, while a retrial date has not yet been set.

title: ‘Biased’ Channel 4 programme on ADHD misrepresented my views, says expert
author: Amelia Hill
content:
A contributor to a controversial Channel 4 documentary on attention deficit hyperactivity disorder has withdrawn her support for the programme, saying it was biased and could lead to an increased suicide risk by encouraging parents to take their children off medication.
Katya Rubia, a professor of cognitive neuroscience at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience at King’s College London, also said The Great ADHD Myth? misrepresented her views.
“I agreed to take part in this documentary because I knew it was aiming to show ADHD was a myth and I wanted to provide an alternative view,” she said. “But they cherrypicked, largely misrepresented, truncated and presented my comments out of context to make them fit into their narrative.
“Biased programmes like this one that push their view of ADHD as a mythical entity are irresponsible and will have detrimental effects, in particular at a time in our society where mental health conditions are escalating and where there is an urgent need for early diagnosis and early treatment to prevent further damage down the line,” she said.
Rubia said ADHD was largely underdiagnosed and undermedicated in the UK. “Parents of children with ADHD may take their children off medication as seen on the programme, which could potentially lead to an increase of the risk of longer-term adverse outcomes of untreated ADHD such as increased anxiety and depression, lower self-esteem, greater risk of substance abuse, suicide, more antisocial behaviour and poorer academic achievement … and reduced employment prospects later in life.”
The Channel 4 programme was presented by the NHS psychiatrist Dr Max Pemberton, who concluded that ADHD was a “social construct” rather than a medical condition, and schools should adapt to better support a wider range of children rather than medicating them into fitting into a restrictive norm.
A Channel 4 spokesperson disputed the claim that it denied the lived experience of those diagnosed with ADHD and instead sought to present the views of a range of senior medical experts who seek to question the conventional understanding of ADHD and if it is a neurodevelopmental condition.
![Mason sits with one hand over his head. He has light brown hair with a side-parted fringe over his forehead and wears a white T-shirt.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/12685f1365ac4a7ebdd332be55fb9174eddadf38/0_0_3456_1405/master/3456.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Rubia criticised the documentary for filming the experience of Mason, a 10-year-old boy, while he was taken off ADHD medication.
“This ‘experiment’ provided nothing but anecdotical evidence confounded by a host of factors,” she said. “The child was not only taken off medication, but also off screens, off additives and junk food, subjected to more nature experience and by implication to more interaction with family, friends and parents.
“This can lead to greater happiness and stronger family bonds (for every child, not just ADHD children). There was also the uncontrolled placebo effect of being treated on TV.”
Rubia said research showed most children preferred to be on medication because they had better control over their emotions as a result and consequently more friends and better relationships with others.
“Substantial research on the effects of nutrition, supplements, exercise, neurofeedback, cognitive training and nature exposure shows unfortunately mostly non-significant or very tiny effects in children with ADHD, very inferior to the effects of medications,” she added.
Rubia also criticised the documentary for its negative portrayal of medication for children with ADHD. “There is substantial evidence that long-term use of medication in ADHD is associated with many benefits such as reduced rates of suicide, comorbidities, crime, traffic accidents and substance abuse.
“The side-effects are relatively minor and benefits are very large compared to other drugs in psychiatry. No mention was made about the potential negative consequences of Mason’s dropping school performance on his self-esteem and academic future,” Rubia said.
The Channel 4 spokesperson said: “We are satisfied that Katya Rubia’s contribution has been edited fairly, is an accurate representation of the interview she gave and that her consent was informed.”
They added: “Whilst the film does not seek to provide answers from one family’s experience, their experiences have opened up discussion around whether today’s world is equipped to accommodate ADHD behaviours and the ethics of medicating these, particularly in children and particularly when the long-term effects remain unknown.
after newsletter promotion
“The welfare of the boy and his family were of paramount importance before, during and after the production process. An independent doctor, his GP, and a health and safety company were consulted. Advice was also taken from three independent psychiatrists on the medication break.”
![Mason and his mother, Shauna.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/d6addc81e0b4637916487553b469f73502b4d783/0_0_3456_1400/master/3456.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Prof Anita Thapar, a clinician scientist at Cardiff University’s school of medicine, who chaired NHS England’s independent ADHD taskforce, also criticised the documentary.
“It’s not a helpful argument to say ADHD is a ‘social construct’,” she said. “The programme did not use experts in clinical research on ADHD or consider all the risks of ADHD that have been shown. It seemed one-sided and used sensational language, such as likening medication to corporal punishment.”
A Channel 4 spokesperson said the channel had a remit to stimulate public debate and challenge the status quo. They added: “Not everyone will agree with everything included in the programme and we acknowledge the strength of feeling that this subject evokes, however there is considerable public debate in this area and testing conventional thinking and exploring different ideas.”
Prof Subodh Dave, the president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, also criticised the programme. “Invalidating the condition does a disservice to people with ADHD and professionals involved in their care,” he said.
A survey launched by the charity ADHD UK after the documentary was screened on Tuesday has received more than 4,000 responses.
More than 94% of respondents said the documentary had increased stigma about ADHD. The same proportion said it was not fair in its representation of ADHD as a condition.
More than 85% said the programme “clearly suggested ADHD is not a real condition” and 88% said it did not make clear that the sceptical views featured were minority views within medicine.
The Channel 4 spokesperson said: “This documentary hears from an extensive range of senior medical experts, with a variance of views on the topic, including, but not limited to, psychiatrists, psychologists, psychotherapists and neuroscientists. Many of these experts work or have worked with the NHS or have held presidential roles at professional membership bodies.
“It is undeniable that there is considerable public debate on various aspects of ADHD, including in relation to the prescribing of medication and diagnostic procedures, and it is not misleading to suggest that these views exist. Channel 4 has a remit which includes offering a platform for alternative views, stimulating public debate and challenging the status quo.”
summary: King's College London professor Katya Rubia has withdrawn her support for a Channel 4 documentary about ADHD, accusing the programme of being biased, misrepresenting her views, and potentially increasing suicide risks by encouraging parents to stop children's medication. Other medical professionals, including the president of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, also criticised the documentary for invalidating the condition and presenting a one-sided argument. Channel 4 defended the programme, stating it fairly represented a range of senior medical experts, followed proper welfare protocols, and aimed to stimulate public debate and challenge conventional thinking.
key_points: Professor Katya Rubia stated that her comments were cherry-picked, truncated, and presented out of context in the Channel 4 documentary The Great ADHD Myth?
Rubia warned that encouraging parents to take children off ADHD medication could lead to severe long-term adverse outcomes, including increased suicide risks and poorer academic achievement.
Channel 4 defended the programme, stating that it was satisfied Rubia's contribution was edited fairly and that the documentary aimed to stimulate public debate on ADHD diagnoses and medication.
Other leading medical figures, such as Prof Subodh Dave and Prof Anita Thapar, also criticised the programme for invalidating ADHD and relying on a one-sided argument.
A survey by the charity ADHD UK found that over 94% of respondents felt the documentary increased stigma and unfairly represented ADHD as a condition.

title: Brandon Flowers: Is fame worth it? I'm not sure anymore
author: Mark Savage
content:
![Brandon Flowers holds a stetson in his right hand and gives a wry look to the camera as he poses outside a stereotypical American motel](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/ca8a/live/32c68bf0-9bd8-11f1-bb4d-1147ef2e78e5.jpg)
Brandon Flowers is on a break from The Killers, with his first solo album in 11 years
- Published
Brandon Flowers has a confession.
For the last 25 years, he's been the frontman of The Killers, channelling his love of stadium rock and British new wave on songs like Mr Brightside, When You Were Young and Human.
But in the back of his mind, there's always been an alternative soundtrack.
"You know, a lot of guys in my line of business develop drug addictions," he says.
"I got a country addiction."
It started when he was a kid in Nephi, Utah. His dad would play Johnny Cash, Merle Haggard and John Conlee on the car stereo. School dances, held at the local golf club, would always feature country and western slow dances.
So when Flowers moved back home and started revisiting his childhood haunts, his passion for country was rekindled.
You can hear the results on his third solo album, Thrasher, recorded in Nashville's famed RCA Studio A - home to Dolly Parton's Jolene and I Will Always Love You - with a group of veteran musicians that included pedal steel legend Bruce Bouton, 85-year-old harmonica player Charlie McCoy, and Americana musician Margo Price.
"I sang live with them and I think they really appreciated that, because it's a very romantic way of doing it," he says.
"It's not something that people do anymore. To actually get that energy down on tape is a different thing."
It's an album he couldn't have made in his 20s.
![Brandon Flowers and Lucy Dacus on stage at the Newport Folk Festival](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/999/cpsprodpb/8c5f/live/6d899390-9bd8-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
The singer previewed his new music at the prestigious Newport Folk Festival, with assistance from singer-songwriter Lucy Dacus
Flowers once said his "experiences weren't interesting enough" to be turned into lyrics. Now, he's excavating his diary to write about his rural upbringing and experiences of working in Las Vegas casinos.
There's also a tribute to his brother-in-law, who died suddenly several years ago and, on Miss America, a critique of the opioid crisis that hit his hometown.
"It's a sad thing, you know? It's basically doctors prescribing people heroin, and it took so many lives unnecessarily."
Prescription painkillers are chemically similar to but not the same as heroin.
He adds: "Even just in my graduating class in that little town, so many of the kids are gone. It's kind of staggering. Such a dirty business."
The album also finds Flowers taking stock of his own life. On American Dream, he fantasises about meeting Elvis Presley (in a flying Tesla, no less) and asking him whether fame and fortune is all it's cracked up to be.
Elvis just laughs - but it's a question that's plagued Flowers for years.
"Sometimes I wonder, what am I trying to achieve, and what am I trying to prove, and who am I trying to prove it to, and what have I gotten from it?" he says.
The song came from a conversation he had with his three teenage sons, "because I worry about them comparing themselves to my success".
Flowers has always been careful to isolate his family from the effects of fame. "We don't talk about it much. There's no gold records hanging in the bathroom or anything like that." And he emphasises that success doesn't automatically bring contentment.
"My dad didn't have that, but is he less happy than me? He may even be more happy than I am.
"He made $25,000 a year and barely got by but he's 82 and he paints, and he goes to garage sales, and he's, like, pumped for that.
"So yeah, I don't know if it's worth it. I don't know anymore."
![Brandon Flowers performs with The Killers at the  UEFA Champions League final. He's dressed in a tuxedo with a bow tie, standing next to a large billboard-style letter K.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/3835/live/d3245190-9bd8-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
The Killers have been on a break since playing the UEFA Champions League final this summer, but Flowers says he has "business in mind" for the band's return
It's easy to understand his ambivalence. Flowers is not your typical rock star. He's quietly spoken and self-effacing. His anecdotes are punctuated with nervous laughter, although he's better at making eye contact than when we first met in the Killers' heyday.
In those interviews, he talked about battling stage fright, and the difficulties of balancing touring commitments with family life.
But as he approaches his 21st wedding anniversary, he says that periodic absences from home can have unexpected benefits.
"There's a danger you could grow apart, but there's also this great rediscovery that can happen, and a freshness it can bring, when you return."
He takes commitment seriously. So seriously, in fact, that he's desperate to make amends for a lyric on the last Killers album, called In Another Life, that made some fans question their relationships.
"In the song, the man is concerned about his situation, and he's asking his wife, 'Am I the man of your dreams, or just a guy from your hometown?'," he explains.
"He's wondering if their proximity is the only reason they're together. And I noticed it was making people look at their relationships in a negative light.
"At one point someone said they got divorced because of this line, and I thought, 'How can I fix this?'"
The answer was to write a new song, Does It Ever Cross Your Mind, that reframed the argument.
"Of all the corners of the universe / We wound up hand in hand," he sings over a twangy banjo. "Some may call it a coincidence / But I prefer design."
![Brandon Flowers in a checked shirt, leaning against a classic American convertible, with fluffy dice hanging from the rear view mirror](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/4665/live/82676a20-9bd9-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
The star will bring his new album to the Royal Albert Hall this autumn
It's one of 23 songs he recorded in Nashville over a period of just three weeks.
Only 10 made the cut for Thrasher. The other 13 are being mixed "in the slowest, slowest possible way" for a separate album, maybe next year.
All this solo activity doesn't mean the end of The Killers, although he admits, "I don't know what the future holds" for the band.
"We're still together, we're still going to make another record [but] there's something beautiful about ageing gracefully," he says.
A student of music history, he knows that longevity requires evolution - and this new batch of country songs could even signpost The Killers' next incarnation.
To put it another way, Flowers can't imagine pretending to be the 20-year-old who wrote Mr Brightside in his friend's bedroom for the rest of his life.
"It's a shame when you see people doing that and trying to hold on," he says. "I always bring up John Lennon or Tom Petty as great examples of [musicians] inhabiting their age."
There's a curious sadness to his predicament. Falling in love with music is a radically different proposition to making it your career; and, like many middle-aged rock bands, The Killers feel beholden to their earliest hits.
![The Killers playing Glastonbury's Pyramid Stage. The photo is taken from the back of the stage, showing Brandon Flowers silhouetted against thousands of flag-waving fans](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/6309/live/a791ba30-9bd9-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
The Killers have headlined Glastonbury twice, most recently in 2019 - when they were joined by Johnny Marr and Pet Shop Boys
Flowers is still grateful to those songs. "It never gets old, feeling the [crowd's] anticipation for When You Were Young, or All These Things That I've Done, or whatever it is."
But the side-effect of spending his life on the stage is that he can no longer enjoy watching other people in concert.
"It's lost the allure to me because that's where I go to work, you know?
"I used to be enthralled. I couldn't believe I was so lucky to be there, seeing Morrissey for the first time, or seeing The Cure for the first time. It was heaven. That feeling is gone."
But he's not despondent. In fact, he's looking forward to touring Thrasher, simply for the joy of playing new material, and re-arranging some of the classics. And there's one band who he thinks could revive his love of live musicâ¦. The band who inspired him to form The Killers in the first place.
"You know what? I was kicking against the Oasis reunion - not because I'm not happy they got back together, but because everyone was just an Oasis fan all of a sudden, even in America, and I sort of railed against it.
"But now I have a son who is 15 who has fallen in love with Oasis. He's learned [their songs] on guitar, and I'll play the piano, rehashing these songs that I loved when I was 19. So I think I would probably feel it again if I went to see Oasis."
Liam and Noel, the ball is in your court.
summary: Brandon Flowers, frontman of The Killers, is releasing his third solo album, a country-influenced record titled Thrasher, recorded in Nashville. During a break from his main band, Flowers has been reflecting on his upbringing, the opioid crisis in his hometown, and whether decades of fame and success have truly been worth it. While he remains uncertain about the future of The Killers and his own relationship with celebrity, he continues to explore new musical directions as he ages.
key_points: Brandon Flowers' new solo album, Thrasher, is heavily influenced by country music and was recorded in Nashville with veteran musicians.
The album features personal themes, including a tribute to his late brother-in-law and a critique of the opioid crisis in his hometown.
Flowers has expressed doubts about whether the fame and fortune from his 25-year career with The Killers are ultimately worth it.
He recorded 23 songs in three weeks, intending to release the surplus tracks on a separate album in the future.
Flowers remains open to the future of The Killers, noting that the new country direction could potentially influence the band's next evolution.

title: ‘The Dog Stars’ World Premiere Red Carpet: Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Rak The Dog & More
author: Glenn Garner
content:
![(L-R) Margaret Qaulley; Rak the dog and Jacob Elordi; Josh Brolin](https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Margaret-Qualley-Jacob-Elordi-Josh-Brolin-3-shot.jpg?w=681&h=383&crop=1) 
London was lit up by The Dog Stars tonight at the world premiere of Ridley Scott’s latest.
On Thursday, Scott and actors Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Josh Brolin and more were among those to walk the red carpet at Odeon Luxe Leicester Square to celebrate the post-apocalyptic sci-fi film, which premieres Aug. 28 in theaters.
Also in attendance was canine co-star Rak Jasper, who appeared alongside Elordi.
In The Dog Stars, onetime pilot Hig (Elordi) teams up with former Marine Bangley (Brolin) to confront the threats of life after a devastating flu pandemic.
Written by Mark L. Smith and based on the 2012 novel by Peter Heller, the Scott-directed movie also stars Allison Janney, Guy Pearce and Benedict Wong.

title: BBC’s Trevor Nelson recovering after brain tumour surgery
author: Nadeem Badshah
content:
Trevor Nelson, the BBC Radio 2 DJ, has revealed he had surgery after being diagnosed with a brain tumour and is now on the mend.
The broadcaster, 62, said in June that he was taking a break from work commitments to deal with health issues.
In a post on Thursday, Nelson said his “world was turned upside down” when he found out he had a brain tumour.
The radio host has spent the last month “recuperating, resting, and recovering” after surgery that went “incredibly well”, and said he hoped to return to work soon.
Nelson, who has spent a 30-year career at the BBC championing Black British music, said in a video message: “A lot of you may have seen the post that I put up at the start of summer, saying that I was stepping back from all my work commitments due to illness.
“There’s been a lot of speculation as to what’s wrong with me, I know that much.”
About 13,000 people in the UK are diagnosed with a primary brain tumour every year, according to the Brain Tumour Charity.
Nelson said: “I’m not going to go into it all now, and I will probably deep-dive into it at a later date so you can hear the whole crazy story.
“But I’ll tell you this: I was minding my own business, and then it was discovered that I had a brain tumour. My world was turned upside down. It was a shock to myself, my close family, and friends. My head was all over the place.”
The broadcaster said he underwent surgery a few weeks after his diagnosis. “Thankfully it went incredibly well, and the last month I’ve been at home recuperating, resting, recovering, and getting some post-op treatment.”
He said he was feeling “almost back to myself”, adding: “I’ve had a really serious situation, but I’ve come out the other side at this point and I feel great. I feel raring to go, and I feel in good health.”
Nelson presented weekdays 2-4pm on Radio 2, and BBC Radio 1Xtra each Sunday from 11am to 1pm before his break. He previously worked for Kiss FM, Radio 1 and MTV.
summary: BBC Radio 2 DJ Trevor Nelson has revealed he underwent successful surgery after being diagnosed with a brain tumour earlier this year. The 62-year-old broadcaster took a break from his work commitments in June to address his health issues. After spending the past month recovering at home, Nelson stated that he feels great, is in good health, and hopes to return to work soon.
key_points: Trevor Nelson revealed he was diagnosed with a brain tumour, which turned his world upside down.
The 62-year-old broadcaster underwent successful surgery a few weeks after his diagnosis.
He has spent the last month at home recuperating, resting, and receiving post-operative treatment.
Nelson stated that he is feeling almost back to himself and hopes to return to his work at the BBC soon.

title: EastEnders boss confirms unexpected twists as Hawkins family arrive in Walford
author: Erin Zammitt
content:
EastEnders spoilers follow.
EastEnders executive producer Ben Wadey has shared more exciting details about the new Hawkins family and what their upcoming arrival in Walford means for Nicola Mitchell. This week, viewers met Nicola’s sisters Gemma and Jodie for the first time, as well as their mum Rose.
Nicola has always been cagey about her past, but she will be forced to confront it head on when in the coming weeks her family land in Albert Square permanently, with Gemma’s husband Ned and son Ryder also about to be introduced.
Related: Best streaming services
Speaking at a recent press event, the soap boss explained just why he wanted to explore fan-favourite Nicola’s backstory and bring in some new and important characters from her life.
"I think she’s such an interesting character, she’d just arrived when I first came in," he said. "Firstly, seeing Dodders’ [actor Laura Doddington] sheer talent, and her amazing performance in every episode.
"I was just fascinated by this woman and the stories that we’ve told with her – this woman who lies so easily, who is responsible for the death of her son’s girlfriend, who so happily sent her husband to prison to protect herself.
"But also she’s fiercely loyal and protective of her children. We discussed in the story office and with writers, what made her that way? I was desperate to uncover those layers and get to know what made Nicola the woman and the mum she is now."
He continued: "Also to give some surprises to the audience, have some things that make us fully ‘get’ her but also understand her in ways perhaps we’re not expecting. The best way to do that is to surround her with people who’ve known her for many, many years.
"So she’s got a very complicated relationship with her mum, and a very nuanced relationship with everybody else. We’ll see that in the coming weeks. There’s going to be quite a lot of change ahead, and things are not all as they seem after the first week or so."
Opening up about the process of creating the Hawkins clan, Ben said: "It’s something you don’t take lightly, it’s a big thing to do. I deliberately waited quite a long time before bringing in a family of this size. I think timing is a really big thing, you want to make sure you have the space in story terms to give all the characters storylines in their own right.
"You need to make sure that when you line up a new unit of characters that each of them have their own story you can tell, and they’re not just floating in the background. So we wanted to make sure that we were confident in the stories we were going to tell with each of them, so timing had to be right."
"And then casting as well is a big old process, you want to get that right," he continued. "As well as all their brilliant performances, you want to make sure there are visuals looks that are similar, and I’m really happy that the casting team did an amazing job – they really do look like they’re all related to each other.
Related: EastEnders appears to confirm Ian Beale's fate in new behind-the-scenes snaps
"It’s also making sure that we’re bringing them in at a period where you want to get to know these characters a bit first, you want to give them good stories and really intrigue everyone, but also get to know them and really care about them and understand who they are before in the months and years ahead, things really do get explosive."
When asked about what is to come for Nicola and her loved ones in the weeks ahead, Ben remarked: "Nicola is not a bad liar, and she’s quite comfortable spinning her own versions of events.
"What I found really interesting as we went through the story was us hearing Nicola’s version, and then us hearing different versions of their past, and what her mum’s version of the past is, compared to her sister’s version of the past.
"It’s so true in so many families, that everybody has these shared, collective experiences and memories of things that happened many years ago but remembers them slightly differently, and it just creates endless drama.
"So if you get those characters right, and the relationships amongst them, it means that we’ll uncover things that maybe will go in directions you weren’t necessarily expecting."

The new arrivals include Nicola's mother Rose, sisters Gemma and Jodie, Gemma's husband Ned, and their son Ryder. Wadey explained that the storyline aims to explore what shaped Nicola's complex character while delivering unexpected twists and dramatic family conflicts.

title: Lawyer for Hayden Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson issues statement
author: Caitlin Hornik
content:
Lawyer for Hayden Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson issues statement
- Actor Hayden Panettiere, known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, died at age 36 in a South Carolina apartment.
- An autopsy showed no signs of trauma, and the official cause of death remains unconfirmed pending toxicology reports that could take up to 12 weeks.
- Panettiere's on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, made the 911 call and turned over a “bag of medication” belonging to Panettiere to police.
- His lawyer, Sloan Ellis from the Ellis Hinton law firm, told TMZ: “Hayden's death remains under investigation and it is important to allow that investigation to proceed.
- It continued: “As has been publicly reported, police confirmed there were no signs of foul play. Out of respect for Hayden's loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time.”
summary: Actor Hayden Panettiere passed away at the age of 36 in South Carolina, with her official cause of death pending toxicology reports. Her on-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, made the 911 call and provided police with a bag of her medication. Hickerson's lawyer issued a statement emphasizing that the investigation is ongoing and that police confirmed no signs of foul play.
key_points: Hayden Panettiere died at age 36 in a South Carolina apartment.
An autopsy showed no signs of trauma, and the cause of death awaits toxicology reports.
Brian Hickerson made the 911 call and gave police a bag of Panettiere's medication.
Hickerson's lawyer released a statement urging respect for the ongoing investigation and noting no signs of foul play.

title: Harry and Meghan’s security funding on UK return is private matter, Burnham says
author: Caroline Davies
content:
Security arrangements for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex while living in the UK are a “private matter”, Andy Burnham has said, after news that Harry and Meghan intend to relocate to Britain from the US this month.
The UK prime minister refused to be drawn on security funding, saying: “This is a private matter. It’s a matter for Harry and Meghan, and we wish them well in the moves that they’re making.”
The couple, who moved to North America more than six years ago, will make their home in a non-royal residence outside London. Their children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are already enrolled at British schools and due to start in September.
King Charles, who was told of the decision on Sunday, is said to welcome the opportunity to see more of his family in a personal capacity. There will be no change in their status as private individuals and non-working royals who do not carry out royal engagements. There is said to be no half-in, half-out option.
Security funding has been a long-running source of tension between Harry and the Home Office, the government department that would decide on such measures. The Times has reported that there are no plans to provide the couple and their family with taxpayer-funded armed protection.
Last year, Harry lost a protracted court battle over what security he and his family would be entitled to while visiting the UK after automatic taxpayer-funded security was withdrawn when the couple stood down as working royals.
During the legal challenge against the Home Office, Harry said in his witness statement: “The UK is my home. The UK is central to the heritage of my children and a place I want them to feel at home as much as where they live at the moment in the US. That cannot happen if it’s not possible to keep them safe when they are on UK soil. I cannot put my wife in danger like that and, given my experiences in life, I am reluctant to unnecessarily put myself in harm’s way too.”
A senior judge later ruled that his “sense of grievance” over the decision about his security was not sufficient as grounds for an appeal.
The prince later told the BBC that he “can’t see a world” in which he would bring his family to the UK.
He was understood to be already awaiting a fresh risk-management assessment, but his new circumstances may now have to be factored in. Decisions on the security of royals are taken by the royal and VIP executive committee, an independent body overseen by the Home Office. The prime minister does not decide about security for the royal family.
After the couple left the UK, Harry was granted a “bespoke” security arrangement. He may no longer qualify for the level of protection he previously had as a working royal but he is a high-profile figure and former military serviceman who has served in Afghanistan, which may be considered in any assessment.
A Home Office spokesperson said: “The UK government’s protective security system is rigorous and proportionate. It is our long-standing policy not to provide detailed information on those arrangements, as doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals’ security.”
In the US, the Sussexes paid for their own private security team.
![Prince Harry and Meghan react to a crowd of people taking photos of the couple on their phones](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/50433cc3f085face8b2018017b5f18395137cfb5/0_0_6000_4001/master/6000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
There has been no statement from the Sussexes on why they are choosing to return to the UK, but a source close to them said they had had a great time during their visit in July, and that “stars are aligning with work” to make this a good time to move. This may include Harry’s Invictus Games, which are to be held in Birmingham next year.
The couple intend to retain their properties in Montecito, California, and in Portugal. Meghan is expected to run her lifestyle brand As Ever from the UK, but it is not yet known whether she will begin undertaking charity visits as a non-working royal or embark on other ventures.
Harry has recently made it clear that he would like to spend more time with his father, who has cancer. Next year also marks the 30th anniversary of the death of his mother, Diana, which will include commemorations and events in the UK. Harry and his family stayed at home of Diana’s family, the Spencers, in Althorp, Northamptonshire, during their visit to the UK last month.
A YouGov poll of 5,810 adults carried out the day after the Sussex’s surprise news, showed 33% believe Harry and Meghan should not return to the UK, while 45% do not know. Less than a quarter (21%) are in favour of the Sussexes relocating to the UK.
summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex intend to relocate from the US to a non-royal residence outside London this month, with their children enrolled in British schools starting in September. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that security arrangements are a private matter, while reports indicate there are no plans to provide taxpayer-funded armed protection. King Charles reportedly welcomes the move, though the couple will remain private individuals and non-working royals without a half-in, half-out option.
key_points: Harry and Meghan plan to relocate back to the UK from the US with their children.
The UK prime minister stated that security funding for the couple is a private matter.
Reports indicate there are no plans to provide taxpayer-funded armed protection for the family.
The couple will retain their status as private individuals and non-working royals.
King Charles was informed of the decision and welcomes the opportunity to see more of his family.

title: Harry and Meghan: the key moments, conflicts and controversies since their US move
author: Guardian staff reporter
content:
Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, will reportedly return to Britain after six years of living in the US, a move that triggered a long period of strained relations with King Charles III, the Prince and Princess of Wales and others in the royal family.
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their two children, Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, are expected to relocate to the UK this month.
The family will reportedly live at a private, non-royal residence outside London, but they plan to maintain their home in California and another property in Portugal.
Here is a timeline charting the major moments since the family moved to the US in 2020.
2020
January
Harry and Meghan announce they will step down as working royals. The decision comes after a period marked by open warfare with the media over claimed intrusion and bullying.
“We intend to step back as ‘senior’ members of the royal family and work to become financially independent, while continuing to fully support Her Majesty the Queen,” the couple say.
June
The couple moves to Meghan’s native California, settling in the wealthy seaside enclave of Montecito near Santa Barbara. Media reports put the 2020 purchase price of their 16-bedroom home at $14.7m.
2021
March
Harry and Meghan are interviewed by Oprah Winfrey on CBS.
In a series of stunning revelations, Meghan accuses the royal family of fostering an atmosphere of racial hostility so intense that she came close to suicide while pregnant with Archie. Meghan also claims members of the royal family had openly expressed concerns about how dark Archie’s skin would be.
In response, Queen Elizabeth issues a statement: “The issues raised, particularly that of race, are concerning. While some recollections may vary, they are taken very seriously and will be addressed by the family privately.”
![Prince Harry and Meghan are interviewed by Oprah Winfrey](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5edd035b0acac397640f40589f799e9945762ffb/0_0_3500_2627/master/3500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
June
The couple’s second child, Lilibet, is born in California. She is named after the family nickname for the Queen.
2022
August
Harry files a lawsuit against the Home Office and the Metropolitan police over his security arrangements in the UK since he stepped down as a working royal.
September
While Harry and Meghan are visiting London, Queen Elizabeth dies. They stay in Britain for her funeral. Ahead of the funeral, Harry and Meghan join William and Kate in meeting wellwishers outside Windsor castle.
![Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, attend the state funeral and burial of Queen Elizabeth](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1158b4c9e21b3f552cfb23a1dfb032821e161b2b/0_0_4576_3074/master/4576.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2023
January
Harry publishes his memoir Spare, detailing his relationship with his family.
Among the most notable revelations, Harry recounts what he says was a physical attack by William as their relationship fell apart over his marriage to Meghan. Describing a confrontation at his London home in 2019, Harry says William called Meghan “difficult”, “rude” and “abrasive”.
May
Harry attends his father’s coronation alone after Meghan and his young children opted not to attend and to remain in California. He walks into Westminster Abbey alone and is seated two rows behind William.
![Prince Harry at the coronation ceremony of King Charles III in Westminster Abbey](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/456937fe5376fa01de79b121c59174bde6c9eed5/0_0_6000_4000/master/6000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
![Prince Harry departs Westminster Abbey during the Coronation of King Charles](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b710c127ff23fb0f5fe5b1f0539c76bfdefeae6f/0_0_5732_3822/master/5732.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2024
February
Buckingham Palace announces King Charles has been diagnosed with a form of cancer and will postpone public engagements to undergo treatment. Harry is photographed arriving at his father’s London residence for a brief meeting.
2025
April
Appearing at a high court appeal over the changes to his police protection, Harry’s lawyer warns his “life is at stake”. The Home Office, defending the appeal, says that Harry’s “bespoke” security arrangements are designed to accommodate his “unique set of circumstances”.
May
Harry loses the legal challenge over his security arrangements, allowing the government to proceed with a “bespoke”, and cheaper, level of protection for his family. Three senior judges reject Harry’s claim he had been “singled out” for “inferior treatment”.
Later that same day, Harry says he wants reconciliation with his family, explaining that his father no longer speaks to him due to the security row.
Speaking in California, Harry says: “I can’t see a world in which I would be bringing my wife and children back to the UK at this point … I miss the UK. And it’s really quite sad I won’t be able to show my children my homeland.”
August
Harry and Meghan sign a fresh deal with Netflix. The couple, who struck a five-year deal in 2020 reportedly worth $100m (£78m), had collaborated with Netflix on a number of projects. Media reports had suggested that poor viewing figures for some of the projects meant that Netflix would not extend the deal.
![Harry and Meghan on a Netflix show](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7d0ab19bfa3f0ba7619134002faf68f442846c91/404_24_1961_1307/master/1961.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
2026
June
Buckingham Palace says Harry will not be staying at the palace during a visit to London, despite the Duke of Sussex’s team earlier announcing publicly he had accepted an invitation to do so.
July
Harry and other high-profile British figures lose their privacy lawsuits against the Daily Mail’s publisher. Harry and the group face a legal bill of up to £50m after losing their case.
![Prince Harry arrives at the Royal Courts of Justice in London](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/35b8b876fc218baf5a79485d8f195a0f896855f9/0_0_4996_3546/master/4996.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
July
King Charles meets in private with Harry and his family, having not seen the children for four years. According to reports, Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet were hosted by Charles and Queen Camilla at the king’s private residence in Gloucestershire.

summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are reportedly planning to relocate from California back to Britain with their two children after six years of living in the US.
